title: An atomic counter
description:
For a single number shared between threads, a mutex is heavier than necessary. `std::atomic<int>` makes each individual operation (`++`, `+=`, read, write) indivisible.

Write `int countTogether(int threads, int perThread)`. It starts that many threads, each of which increments one shared `std::atomic<int>` `perThread` times, and returns the final value. No mutex.
hints: Create `std::atomic<int> count{ 0 };`, start the threads with a lambda that captures it by reference and does `++count` in a loop, join them, and return `count.load()`.
unitTests:
TEST("every increment counts") { for (int round{ 0 }; round < 5; ++round) CHECK_EQ(countTogether(8, 25000), 200000); }
TEST("edge cases") { CHECK_EQ(countTogether(1, 10), 10); CHECK_EQ(countTogether(0, 10), 0); CHECK_EQ(countTogether(4, 0), 0); }
